title: Mermin-Peres magic rectangles modulo odd primes
authors: Josse van Dobben de Bruyn, Remy van Dobben de Bruyn, Peter Zeman
abstract: The Mermin-Peres magic square provides a simple example of a system of linear equations over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ which has no classical solutions but does have a finite-dimensional operator solution. For a long time, it was not known how to construct similar examples over $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$ with $d$ odd. In this paper, we construct, for every integer $d\ge2$, a linear system over $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$ that has a finite-dimensional operator solution but no classical solution. For an odd prime $p$, our operators act on two $p$-dimensional qudits and generate a finite $p$-group obtained by adjoining diagonal polynomial phase operators to the generalized Pauli group. Classical inconsistency follows from an elementary linearity argument comparing assignments on abelian subgroups.
summary: This paper constructs explicit examples of quantum constraint systems over $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$ that violate classical realism, extending the Mermin-Peres paradox to arbitrary odd moduli. The authors use group theory and advanced algebraic techniques to prove the existence of these systems, demonstrating that quantum correlations persist even when the underlying algebra is not based on $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. This is significant for understanding the limits of local realism in generalized quantum systems.
main_problem: To construct linear constraint systems over $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$ (for odd $d$) that possess a solution in the operator algebra but no corresponding classical solution, generalizing the Mermin-Peres paradox.
main_result: The authors prove that such systems exist for every integer $d \ge 2$, providing a constructive proof that contradicts previous conjectures regarding odd moduli.
method: The proof involves constructing the system using generalized Pauli operators acting on qudits and employing an elementary linearity argument comparing assignments on abelian subgroups to show classical inconsistency.
model_or_system: The model is a linear system $Ax=b$ defined over $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$. The operators are constructed using generalized Pauli matrices acting on two $p$-dimensional qudits, forming a finite $p$-group $G_{p,d}$.
key_observables: The existence of a group-valued solution versus the non-existence of a classical assignment satisfying the constraints.
important_parameters: The modulus $d$ (specifically odd primes $p$), the dimension of the qudits ($p$), and the structure of the underlying finite $p$-group $G_{p,d}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis for the prime case relies on the structure of the group $G_{p, p-1}$ and the application of a general linearity criterion (Lemma 5.1) derived from difference equations.
figures_summary: The text notes the inclusion of large matrices illustrating concrete examples of Mermin-Peres magic rectangles over $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general existence theorem for all $d \ge 2$. For the prime case, it develops advanced mathematical tools, including a linearity criterion (Lemma 5.1), which is then applied to prove that the required function $\lambda$ must vanish on a specific element $J$ (Theorem 5.2).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fundamental questions about the boundary between quantum correlations (operator solutions) and classical correlations (local hidden variable theories) in generalized settings beyond qubits.
